claim_annotations.claim_text: The client attends lectures but leaves before small-group discussions because of worry about saying something foolish and being noticed.

evidence.evidence_text: I still attend the lectures, but I leave before the small-group conversations.
evidence.speaker: Client

evidence.evidence_text: I worry I will say something foolish and everyone will notice.
evidence.speaker: Client

claim_annotations.assessment_rationale: The client directly reports both leaving before group discussions and the stated worry. The connection is supported by their immediate answer to what makes them leave.

claim_annotations.claim_text: Rehearsing a question until the discussion ends and imagining negative evaluation may be contributing to avoidance.

evidence.evidence_text: Last week I had a question, but I kept rehearsing it in my head until the discussion ended.
evidence.speaker: Client

evidence.evidence_text: I picture them looking at each other or thinking I should already know the answer.
evidence.speaker: Client

claim_annotations.assessment_rationale: The client reports the rehearsal, imagined judgment, and a missed opportunity to speak. These details support the interpretation, though the client does not explicitly state that the thoughts caused the broader pattern of leaving.

claim_annotations.claim_text: The client believes all classmates have rejected them.

evidence.evidence_text: One person asked if I wanted to get coffee after class, but I said I was busy.
evidence.speaker: Client

claim_annotations.assessment_rationale: The client does not report believing that all classmates have rejected them and cannot recall a negative response; a classmate’s invitation is contrary to the claim of universal rejection.

claim_annotations.claim_text: The group difficulty reflects a broader inability to speak comfortably with others.

evidence.evidence_text: I feel it most in groups. I can talk comfortably with my cousin one-on-one.
evidence.speaker: Client

claim_annotations.assessment_rationale: The client explicitly distinguishes group situations from one-on-one conversation and reports being comfortable with a cousin, which does not support a broad inability to speak with others.

claim_annotations.claim_text: This pattern began after repeated bullying in childhood.
claim_annotations.assessment_rationale: The transcript contains no report of childhood bullying or information about when the pattern began.

model_formulation: The client attends lectures but leaves before small-group discussions, describing worry about saying something foolish and being noticed. Rehearsing a question until the discussion ends and imagining negative evaluation may be contributing to avoidance. The client believes all classmates have rejected them, and the group difficulty may reflect a broader inability to speak comfortably with others. This pattern began after repeated bullying in childhood.
session_transcript:
T1 Client: I have been skipping the discussion portion of my evening course. I still attend the lectures, but I leave before the small-group conversations.
T2 Therapist: What makes you leave at that point?
T3 Client: I worry I will say something foolish and everyone will notice.
T4 Client: Last week I had a question, but I kept rehearsing it in my head until the discussion ended.
T5 Therapist: What do you imagine people would do if you asked it?
T6 Client: I picture them looking at each other or thinking I should already know the answer.
T7 Therapist: Has anyone in the group responded negatively to you?
T8 Client: Not that I can recall. One person asked if I wanted to get coffee after class, but I said I was busy.
T9 Therapist: Do you remember feeling this way in other settings?
T10 Client: I feel it most in groups. I can talk comfortably with my cousin one-on-one.
